newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD was undervalued - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD was undervalued - paper.

text.p: Brazilian state mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), which is soon to be privatized, was undervalued, Jornal do Brasil daily said on Monday.

The newspaper said Vale is worth 12 billion reais, above the minimum price of 10.3 billion reais set by the federal government for the company, according to a study by a group of 22 experts from Rio de Janeiro Federal University (UFRJ).

The group, headed by physicist Luis Pinguelli Rosa, examined Vale's documents available to investors at the so-called Data Room following a request from a lower house committee, Jornal do Brasil said.

The newspaper said the information available at the Data Room contrasts to data provided by Vale. It said the Data Room leaves out information about two mines of uranium at Carajas region that the group visited.
Jornal do Brasil daily said the group questioned Merrill Lynch's evaluation of the company, noting that Carajas' iron ore was undervalued by 65 percent.
Merrill Lynch led one of the consortia hired to evaluate the firm and propose a privatization model for CVRD.
According to Pinguelli, Merrill Lynch's report virtually limits CVRD to an iron ore mining company, Jornal do Brasil said.
